evidence.claim: A desert road follows the Salt River toward Roosevelt Dam.
evidence.quote: The route follows the Salt River northeast to the Theodore Roosevelt Dam

evidence.claim: The Apache Trail corridor takes SR 88 from Apache Junction through desert terrain toward Roosevelt Dam.
evidence.quote: It runs from U.S. Route 60 (US 60) in Apache Junction through desert terrain to SR 188 near Roosevelt Dam.

evidence.claim: Two lanes lead into Tonto National Forest and along Canyon Lake’s southern shore; beyond Tortilla Flat, an unpaved section winds through the Superstition Mountains.
evidence.quote: SR 88 nears Canyon Lake south of the Mormon Flat Dam and follows a part of the southern shore of Canyon Lake.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia identifies part of SR 88 as the state-designated Apache Trail Historic Road and the eastern corridor as a National Forest Scenic Byway.
evidence.quote: Part of SR 88, known as the Apache Trail Historic Road, is one of only four state designated Historic Roads under the Arizona Parkways, Historic and Scenic Roads program.

evidence.claim: At Tortilla Flat, road building and dam building were linked: the settlement served freight haulers heading to Roosevelt Dam’s construction site in 1904.
evidence.quote: Based on available records, Tortilla Flat got its start because of the road construction to Roosevelt Dam in 1904. There was a need for a stagecoach stop for freight haulers on their way to the construction site at Roosevelt Dam and Tortilla Flat served that purpose.

evidence.claim: Tourists and mail carriers later used its stage stop through the 1930s.
evidence.quote: At that point Tortilla Flat was a stage stop for tourists and mail carriers through the 1930s.

evidence.claim: The route received the number 88 in 1927; paving reached the Apache Junction-to-Canyon Lake section in the late 1940s.
evidence.quote: The number 88 was given to the route by 1927

evidence.claim: In 2019, the Woodbury Fire and subsequent flooding damaged the unpaved road, closing the section between mileposts 222 and 229.
evidence.quote: Following the 2019 Woodbury Fire and subsequent damage to the unpaved portion of the route due to catastrophic flooding from the remnants of Hurricane Lorena, the road was closed from milepost 222 to 229

evidence.claim: From Apache Junction, the road passes Goldfield before entering the national forest and reaching Canyon Lake.
evidence.quote: Passing a ghost town known as Goldfield, Apache Trail enters Tonto National Forest

evidence.claim: After Tortilla Flat, the corridor winds east, approaches Apache Lake and follows the Salt River northeast to Roosevelt Dam.
evidence.quote: It passes through the town of Tortilla Flat, becoming an unpaved dirt trail winding eastward through the Superstition Mountains. SR 88 again turns northeast and nears Apache Lake. The route follows the Salt River northeast to the Theodore Roosevelt Dam

evidence.claim: The highway once continued toward Globe, but that eastern extension became SR 188 in 1999.
evidence.quote: An eastern extension of State Route 88 to Globe, Arizona was redesignated as State Route 188 on August 20, 1999.

evidence.claim: Pavement returns near the dam, and SR 88 meets SR 188 beside Roosevelt Lake.
evidence.quote: near which the route is again paved. SR 88 intersects with SR 188 along the coast of Theodore Roosevelt Lake.

flags: Partial designation reporting: all cached pages are Wikipedia. No ADOT, Forest Service or tourism page supplies the designating body’s description or rationale; the old ADOT source is absent. National Forest Scenic Byway is supported by 00; 04 instead calls it a National Scenic Byway. Used 00, flagged the naming discrepancy.

Road origins conflict: 00 says mid-1920s, 01/12 connects road construction to dam freight in 1904, and 03 says constructed by Youngberg in 1905. Distinguished the freight settlement from the 1927 highway number; underlying construction records are needed. Dropped the categorical claim that the entire road was cut in 1904.

Dropped the claim that most of Fish Creek Bridge-to-Roosevelt Lake has never been paved: its cited ADOT page is not cached. Also dropped the blanket claim that all the remaining road is dirt: 00 says pavement returns near Roosevelt Dam.

Access needs road-manager verification before publication. Only Wikipedia 00 describes the September 2024 reopening and vehicle restriction; it does not clearly bound the restriction. The practical note attributes that report without promising current through access. Checked date is cache review only.

The old practical note’s claim that the road is narrow is not expressly supported in this cache; omitted. The old post-office and voting-precinct claim is embedded in a questionable attributed population superlative in 01; omitted pending a direct source.
Dam page 10 gives conflicting construction starts, 1905 and 1903. Neither is used; completion and later reconstruction are distinguished.
